newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel to propose land policy changes.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel to propose land policy changes.

text.p: An influential Japanese government panel is calling for a change in the nation's land policy to seek more effective use of land and to increase liquidity of real estate holdings.
A National Land Agency official said the advisory panel on land policy would hand over its proposal later on Thursday to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
According to a draft report made available to reporters, the panel is urging an "appropriate" tax on landholdings in line with balanced assessments of value.
It also supports a long-term, stable tax system, aiming to promote effective use of land. It did not however, make specific proposals on the current taxation system on landholdings.
It also urged steps to encourage small landowners to sell their land or cooperate in development projects in order for large-scale development to take place in big cities.
To promote effective use of land, the draft report called for the establishment of fund-raising steps, such as real estate securitisation, project finance and joint venture projects.
Land prices had fallen to a point where the price surges in the latter half of the 1980s "bubble economy" had been offset after a five-year slump, the draft report said.
Despite a five-year tailspin in the property market, analysts say there are no signs land prices have bottomed out.
The draft said that emergency intervention measures to curb land prices adopted in 1991 were no longer needed as land prices were still falling.
It is the first time in five years that the government has reviewed Japan's basic land policy.
